People already affected by disasters and economic instability could face greater needs. Existing vulnerability may increase harmful coping; no dated rationale update establishes later outcomes.
questions: Which areas had the least recovery from earlier shocks before the forecast drought?
What evidence separates anticipated disease risks from confirmed outbreaks?

assessment.text: Dry conditions during the growing season could compound earlier humanitarian shocks.

impact.text: Lower yields and water scarcity could worsen food insecurity, WASH needs, and disease risks.

vulnerability.text: Existing needs increase the risk of reduced meals and other harmful coping responses.
